newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator pleased with impact of Iran sanctions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator pleased with impact of Iran sanctions.

text.p: After months of calling on the Clinton administration to enforce a law passed last August for tighter sanctions against Iran, U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato Tuesday hailed the administration for making the sanctions work.
"I applaud the administration for working to make the sanctions stick, and I urge them to remain vigilant," D'Amato said in a statement.
The statement followed comments Tuesday by a senior member of the Iranian parliament's oil commission, Mohsen Yahyavi, who said the sanctions had slowed foreign investments.
"Despite widespread arrangements by the (oil) ministry, foreign contractors are not much interested in engaging in petroleum projects in Iran," Yahyavi was quoted as saying by the daily Iran News.
D'Amato spearheaded the law last year which called for the United States to punish non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more a year in Iranian or Libyan oil and gas projects.
"The Iranians are admitting what we knew would happen. The sanctions are making it harder for them to get access to western currency," D'Amato said.

Since August, he has written several letters to the White House urging the administration to use the law against Turkey, Malaysia's state oil company Petronas, and Pakistan, who announced plans to invest in or buy natural gas from Iran.
The administration has not yet said whether the law would apply in any of the cases.
But an aide to D'Amato praised the administration's efforts to talk to the countries involved.
"From everything that I've been able to tell, they are trying. There have been no other violations," the aide said.
"It's even working in Libya," he said. "The deals that are being signed are under the $40 million limit."
